Senses.Note: Host and guest exchange roles names a reversible encounter relation, not a permanent reassignment of personal identities. The records apply it both to paired case figures and to the responsive operation expected of a capable practitioner.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Host and guest exchange roles when the initiative and responsive positions in an encounter can reverse without losing their distinction.
EvidenceBody: Hongzhi Zhengjue says that Buddha and Caoshan exchange host and guest while each has an eye for appearance before and after emergence. Xuedou Chongxian says that an eye at the hundred-foot pole enables host and guest to exchange and enter the tiger's cave. Hanyue Fazang joins the exchange to whole-body taking and releasing by Linji's true descendants. In another raised encounter, Hongzhi calls Tianxian and Piyun's exchange clear in its entrances and exits. Together the cases support reversible encounter roles rather than a generic change of identities.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Commentators use the formula to judge whether encounter partners can reverse initiative and response with clear entrances, exits, taking, and releasing.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase does not erase the two roles or claim that every dialogue contains a successful exchange; several witnesses explicitly make the exchange conditional on an eye or capable strategy.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All four passages name the same reversible host-guest relation, whether applied to a case pair or stated as an encounter capacity.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Switch places renders the same relational reversal in less technical English without collapsing host and guest into fixed people.

ModifierControls.Finding: The corpus couples exchange with entrances and exits, whole-body taking and releasing, and an eye capable of the move.

FamilyControls.Finding: The paired roles remain distinct even when reversed; generic role change or identity exchange is broader than the attested formula.
